papers.title: Memory Self-Awareness Phenotypes are Associated with Alzheimers Disease Biomarker Burden and Clinical Progression in Amnestic Mild Cognitive Impairment
papers.abstract: Background: Altered memory self-awareness is common in mild cognitive impairment (MCI), but its relationship to Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology and progression remains unclear. Methods: Using 590 amnestic MCI ADNI participants, memory self-awareness was derived from participant-informant discrepancies on the memory subdomain of the Everyday Cognition questionnaire. Heightened awareness and unawareness subscores were calculated, and k-means clustering identified four phenotypes. Associations with cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and positron emission tomography (PET) were examined, and clinical progression was assessed using Cox models. Results: Aware and Unaware groups showed lower CSF amyloid-B, and higher CSF phosphorylated tau and PET amyloid. The Unaware phenotype was associated with increased progression risk (hazard ratio 2.41, 95% CI 1.48-3.92), whereas the Worried Well phenotype showed reduced risk (hazard ratio 0.58, 95% CI 0.34-0.99). Conclusions: Multidimensional assessment of memory self-awareness identifies biologically and prognostically distinct subgroups within MCI and may improve risk stratification in prodromal AD.

papers.title: Suvorexant Inversely Affects Phosphorylated Tau in Human Cerebrospinal Fluid and Plasma
papers.abstract: Alzheimer disease (AD) is characterized by amyloid-{beta} plaques and neurofibrillary tangles of tau. Suvorexant, a dual orexin receptor antagonist, was previously shown to acutely reduce the ratio of phosphorylated tau-181 to unphosphorylated tau-181 (pT181/T181) in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). However, its effects on plasma pT181/T181 and broader proteomic networks remain unknown. Here, we conducted a secondary analysis of samples from a randomized, placebo-controlled trial of 25 participants receiving placebo or suvorexant 20 mg. Paired CSF and plasma samples were collected longitudinally via indwelling intrathecal and intravenous catheters. Plasma AD biomarkers were quantified by mass spectrometry, and proteomic profiling was performed using the SomaScan 11K assay on samples from hours 0, 16, and 24. Suvorexant increased pT181/T181 in plasma while decreasing it in CSF between 08:00 to 16:00. At the pathway level, suvorexant increased the extracellular abundance of proteins associated with translation, RNA binding, cytoskeletal organization and endosomal sorting, centrally at 16 hours and peripherally at 24 hours, and decreased cytokine and receptor-ligand signaling and serine protease activity in plasma at 24 hours. As plasma biomarkers are increasingly used for clinical screening and trial enrollment, factors that influence their levels, including medications, must be identified and their effects on interpretation understood.

papers.title: False-Positive Calls of Reimplemented Published Analyses for Covert Command-Following on Electroencephalograms Recorded Without Study Commands
papers.abstract: Objective: To measure how often published electroencephalographic analyses for covert command-following call patients positive without commands, and their detection of genuine responses. Methods: This cross-sectional study applied 11 reimplemented published analyses to electroencephalograms without commands: 974 clinical electroencephalography patients and, with rules fixed, 730 new patients; 38 with prolonged disorders of consciousness; and 544 comatose patients after cardiac arrest. Outcomes: false calls (share called positive) against a 5% benchmark, and genuine-response detection. Results: Three of 10 command-following analyses called significantly more than 5% of clinical electroencephalography patients positive, replicated in new patients: Goldfine 2011, a spectral test, 23.3% (95% CI, 20.2%-26.6%), above its stated 5%; du Bois 2026, a criterion for entry to brain-computer interface training, 22.2% (95% CI, 19.2%-25.5%); and Guger 2018, a P300 accuracy threshold, 13.8% (95% CI, 11.5%-16.3%), near its approximate 12% chance rate (24.5% over 2 runs). The other 7 called 0.0% to 6.9%. After cardiac arrest: 11.5% to 27.3%. All 3 detected genuine responses. Identified contributors: a variance ignoring within-command dependence (Goldfine 2011), selection over configurations and times (du Bois 2026) and a permissive threshold (Guger 2018). Goldfine 2011's command-level correction, fixed before testing, called 0.8% of new patients and 2.4% after arrest, detecting 93.4% of stroke imagery-versus-rest sessions but few between imagery types. Interpretation: Reimplemented published analyses called up to 27% of patients positive without commands, more with repeated runs. A positive result needs its complete call rule's false-call rate and detection at that rate; imagery-versus-rest detection may reflect task engagement, not imagery. Funding: A.G. and E.K. were supported by the Clinical and Translational Science Awards (CTSA) Grant UL1TR002541 from the National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences, through the Harvard Catalyst - The Harvard Clinical and Translational Science Center Pilot Award Program. The content is solely the responsibility of the authors and does not necessarily represent the official views of the National Institutes of Health.

papers.title: Olfactory Function in Preclinical Alzheimer's Disease: A Multi-Cohort Study
papers.abstract: Introduction: Olfactory impairment is an early feature of Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, it is unclear if olfactory performance reflects early pathological changes during preclinical AD and/or predicts subsequent clinical progression among characterized cognitively normal (CN) individuals. We aimed to determine whether odor identification differs by amyloid status, relates to medial temporal lobe (MTL) tau burden and morphometry, and predicts longitudinal conversion to mild cognitive impairment (MCI). Methods: We analyzed data from 257 cognitively normal (CN) older adults enrolled in PREVENT-AD (n = 217) and UCLouvain (n = 40), including 76 amyloid-positive (CN A+) and 181 amyloid-negative participants (CN A-). Participants completed olfactory testing, underwent tau-PET imaging, and structural MRI. Results: CN A+ participants had significantly lower odor identification performance than CN A- participants, with no evidence of cohort heterogeneity. Tau-PET associations with odor identification differed by cohort. After whole-brain FDR correction and exclusion of extreme values, parahippocampal tau burden was negatively associated with odor identification score in UCLouvain ([18F]MK-6240), an association that was not found in PREVENT-AD ([18F]flortaucipir). No morphometric association survived multiple comparison correction. In 250 participants with longitudinal follow-up, each 10-percentage-point higher odor identification score was associated with a 16% lower hazard of incident MCI, independent of baseline global cognition and APOE {epsilon}4-carrier status. Discussion: Odor identification was lower in preclinical AD and associated with incident MCI independently of baseline global cognition and APOE {epsilon}4-carrier status. Its association with parahippocampal tau burden differed between cohorts, supporting further investigation using harmonized imaging methods.

papers.title: CSF PrP-amyloid seeding predicts clinical onset in inherited prion disease
papers.abstract: Silent proteopathic seed propagation is hypothesised to precede neurodegenerative disease, but direct evidence that it signals near-term clinical conversion in humans is lacking. In prion disease, a prototypic disorder of proteopathic seeding, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) real-time quaking-induced conversion (RT-QuIC) offers a direct measure of prion protein amyloid seeding activity. We analysed longitudinal CSF RT-QuIC data from 94 PRNP E200K mutation carriers across international natural history cohorts to determine whether seeding status predicts clinical conversion. Eleven carriers developed inherited prion disease; all showed at least one positive RT-QuIC result before onset. First positivity appeared a median of 2.0 years prior to symptoms (IQR 1.3-3.3; range 0.2-4.8). Landmark analyses showed RT-QuIC positivity identified a markedly increased short-term conversion risk, whereas persistently asymptomatic carriers remained negative throughout follow-up. These findings establish CSF RT-QuIC positivity as a biomarker-defined state of incipient conversion in E200K carriers, informing risk stratification and preventive trial design.

papers.title: Stage-Specific Roles of Plasma GFAP in Linking Amyloid Cascade in Alzheimer Disease
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Astrocytic reactivity, measured by plasma glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), is robustly elevated across the Alzheimer disease (AD) continuum, yet its relationship with the amyloid cascade remains poorly understood. METHODS: We integrated plasma GFAP with multimodal AD biomarkers, including cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) or plasma amyloid-beta (Abeta42/40), amyloid and tau positron emission tomography (PET), structural MRI, and clinical severity, across a discovery cohort (Knight Alzheimer Disease Research Center, n=278) and an independent replication cohort (Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, n=236). RESULTS: In the overall samples of both cohorts, plasma GFAP statistically mediated the associations between soluble Abeta42/40 and amyloid PET and between amyloid PET and tau PET; both remained significant after false discovery rate (FDR) correction. In tau-negative individuals, the indirect association between soluble Abeta42/40 and amyloid PET remained significant after correction only in Knight ADRC. In amyloid-positive individuals, the indirect association between amyloid PET and tau PET remained significant after correction only in ADNI. Interaction findings were not consistently replicated across cohorts, either before or after correction. Plasma proteomics identified a GFAP-associated protein network enriched for extracellular matrix and immune-related pathways. DISCUSSION: These findings support associations of plasma GFAP with amyloid and tau biomarkers within A/T-defined groups and identify GFAP-associated extracellular matrix and inflammatory protein signatures that warrant further investigation.

papers.title: Epilepsy Lateralization by Elastic Net Regularization of a Diffusion Tensor Imaging Biomarker using Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Objective: Accurate lateralization of the epileptogenic focus is essential for presurgical evaluation of patients with drug-resistant epilepsy. This study examined whether diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) measures of white matter microstructure, combined with clinical and demographic variables, could classify epilepsy lateralization using machine learning. Methods: We present a retrospective analysis of 334 adult patients undergoing presurgical epilepsy evaluation at the University of Kansas Health System. Fractional anisotropy (FD) and mean diffusivity (MD) were extracted from 36 bilateral white matter tracts and combined with clinical and demographic variables. Several supervised machine learning approaches were evaluated, with elastic net logistic regression selected for detailed analysis. Models classified right-sided, left-sided, and bilateral or generalized epilepsy. Performance was evaluated with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity as performance metrics. Results: Elastic net models demonstrated good discrimination across classification tasks, with AUC values ranging from 0.76 to 0.88. The strongest performance distinguished left-sided epilepsy from bilateral or generalized epilepsy (AUC = 0.88; accuracy = 0.90; sensitivity = 0.90; specificity = 0.89). Discrimination between unilateral epilepsy and bilateral or generalized epilepsy was also good (AUC = 0.83). Classification of right-sided versus left-sided epilepsy demonstrated lower performance (AUC = 0.76). Significance: DTI-derived white matter features analyzed using a machine learning approach may provide complementary information for epilepsy lateralization during presurgical evaluation. Further studies incorporating other pre-surgical evaluation data into the machine learning model are needed to establish the clinical utility of this approach.

papers.title: Functional Heritability Partitioning, Multi-Tissue Transcriptomic Colocalization, and Pharmacogenomic Target Deconvolution Across 127 Alzheimer's Disease Susceptibility Loci
papers.abstract: Background: The landmark genome-wide association meta-analysis of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and AD-by-proxy across N = 2,815,127 individuals (Uffelmann et al., Nature, 2026) expanded the known susceptibility landscape to 127 independent genomic risk loci (160 association signals) and established an autosomal common-variant SNP heritability of h2_SNP = 16.0% on the liability scale. Translating these 127 static statistical signals into pathway-stratified clinical trials requires resolving three quantitative gaps: how the non-APOE polygenic architecture partitions across distinct cellular programs, which effector genes operate via cortical parenchymal versus peripheral myeloid gene expression, and which targets possess nanomolar human bioactivity suitable for genetically stratified trials. Methods: Operating entirely on individual-genotype-free summary statistics structured along a previously established tridimensional diagnostic framework (Axis 1: Etiology and Genetic Architecture; Axis 2: Molecular Pathophysiology and Biomarker Programs; Axis 3: Neuroanatomical-Cognitive Topography; Menendez-Gonzalez, Alzheimers Dement, 2025), we ingested the complete NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog build GCST90695466 (8,159,496 autosomal and 160,704 X-chromosome variants). First, we performed functional heritability partitioning via stratified excess chi-square inflation and additive genetic variance (sum 2pq*beta^2) across +/-50 kb cis-regulatory windows of 50 fine-mapped effector genes organized into five mechanistic Axis 2 programs (MICROGLIAL_IMMUNE, PROTEOPATHY_AUTOPHAGY, ENDOCYTIC_VESICULAR, SYNAPTIC_CALCIUM, and MITOCHONDRIAL_OXIDATIVE). Second, we conducted Summary-data-based Mendelian Randomization (SMR) and Approximate Bayes Factor colocalization (PP.H4) across 54 human tissues in GTEx v10 (4,415 matched cis-eQTLs) alongside Open Targets v4 SuSiE fine-mapped credible sets spanning ROS/MAP dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), BrainSeq, primary human monocytes, and UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project (UKB-PPP) plasma pQTLs. Third, we queried EMBL-EBI ChEMBL v34 across 2,785 human bioactivity assays (IC50, Ki, Kd, EC50) and Open Targets tractability matrices to construct an empirical pharmacogenomic target atlas. Results: Across 8,159,496 autosomal variants, the genome-wide mean test statistic was chi2_GW = 1.5099. Outside the APOE/TOMM40 super-locus (max chi2 = 3,267.15; 2pq*beta^2 = 0.0882, accounting for 74.82% of top-locus additive variance), 89,589 cis-regulatory SNPs across 48 non-APOE effector genes exhibited a 12.88-fold heritability enrichment over the autosomal background. Normalized across the 16.0% polygenic liability scale, non-APOE functional heritability concentrated in MICROGLIAL_IMMUNE (39.22% share; h2_SNP = 6.28%; 13.02x enrichment; mean chi2 = 7.64) and PROTEOPATHY_AUTOPHAGY (36.34% share; h2_SNP = 5.81%; 14.98x enrichment; mean chi2 = 8.64), followed by ENDOCYTIC_VESICULAR (16.71% share; h2_SNP = 2.67%; 12.69x enrichment; mean chi2 = 7.47), SYNAPTIC_CALCIUM (5.40% share; h2_SNP = 0.86%; 10.05x enrichment; mean chi2 = 6.13), and MITOCHONDRIAL_OXIDATIVE (2.33% share; h2_SNP = 0.37%; 5.24x enrichment; mean chi2 = 3.67). Multi-tissue SMR and colocalization resolved a striking divergence between Axis 3 cortical parenchyma and myeloid compartments: QPCT (rs2300880; Z_SMR = -4.62, p_SMR = 3.93e-6, PP.H4_cis = 0.919, PP.H4_local = 0.994 in Brain_Cortex; PP.H4_local = 0.979 in Brain_Frontal_Cortex_BA9) and AXL (rs12979764; p_SMR = 2.13e-4, PP.H4_cis = 0.902, PP.H4_local = 0.924 in Brain_Cortex) colocalized directly within human cerebral cortex and ROS/MAP DLPFC. Conversely, canonical myeloid and endocytic drivers (BIN1, CD33, TREM2, INPP5D, SYK) exhibited near-zero bulk cortical eQTL colocalization (PP.H4_cis <= 0.025 in Brain_Cortex) despite high SuSiE Locus-to-Gene scores (L2G = 0.875-0.968) and robust colocalization in primary monocytes and spleen (INPP5D PP.H4_local = 0.992; BIN1 PP.H4_local = 0.999). ChEMBL v34 bioactivity profiling confirmed low-nanomolar human target potency for clinical-stage compounds across all five programs, including isradipine (2.0 nM) and nilvadipine (19.0 nM) for CACNA1S, omaveloxolone (2.2 nM) for KEAP1, fostamatinib/R406 (41.0 nM) for SYK, and varoglutamstat/PQ912 (61.0 nM) for QPCT. Conclusion: Over three-quarters (75.56%) of the non-APOE common-variant heritability of Alzheimer's disease resides within microglial immune surveillance and proteopathic clearance networks. If prospectively validated in genotype-stratified clinical cohorts, these empirical summary-statistics findings suggest that therapeutic efficacy in sporadic AD may depend on matching pathway-selective drugs to a patient's individual Functional Pathway Burden Score rather than administering uniform monotherapies to genetically unstratified populations.

papers.title: PRISM-AD quantifies clinical and genetic contributions to cognitive risk prediction
papers.abstract: Background: Older adults with high inherited Alzheimer's disease (AD) susceptibility can still be cognitively normal (CN). An overall risk estimate alone does not show the cognitive and genetic contributions within a forecast. Objective: To quantify clinical and genetic contributions to cognitive prognosis. Methods: PRISM-AD combined nonlinear clinical functions and a polygenic risk score (PRS) term in 4,435 European-ancestry participants. Participant-level internal validation evaluated first recorded mild cognitive impairment (MCI) after CN in 908 participants and AD dementia after MCI in 714, within three or five years. Separately fitted comparators used identical inputs. Post hoc clinical-course comparisons used regression with robust standard errors and Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) correction. Results: PRISM-AD using current assessments achieved average precision of 0.2996 and 0.4094 for three- and five-year CN-to-MCI, with estimates close to logistic regression. No PRISM-AD PRS increment met BH q < 0.05. Three-year first-MCI forecasts characterized risk contributions in 893 initially CN participants. A retrospective comparison over available follow-up included 95 participants with later AD and 701 with CN at their last diagnostic assessment. Modeled genetic factors were higher in later AD in nine of ten shared cognitive-risk deciles. After adjustment for modeled cognitive risk and fold, the genetic-factor ratio was 1.135 (nominal 95% CI, 1.073 to 1.201, BH q < 0.001). Conclusions: Higher genetic contributions were associated with later AD at comparable modeled cognitive risk. These exploratory profiles require independent validation before use in cognitive follow-up or prevention research.

papers.title: A Reproducible Decomposed Large Language Model Pipeline for Structured Abstraction of Multimodal Neuroimaging Reports: Development and Independent Validation in 1,669 Emergency Department Encounters for Dizziness and Vertigo
papers.abstract: Objective: To develop and independently validate a decomposed, modality-specific large language model (LLM) pipeline that abstracts structured variables from the free-text neuroimaging reports of a multimodal stroke workup, and to validate the resulting structured dataset for reuse in downstream research. Materials and Methods: A frozen pipeline (temperature 0) extracting 22 variables across CT head, CT angiography, CT perfusion, and MRI brain was applied to 1,669 ED encounters for dizziness or vertigo; 11 variables were pre-specified as primary (Tier 1). Reproducibility used three same-session runs and a nine-week repeat run; three frontier models (Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.4, Gemini 3.5 Flash) measured cross-model agreement (Cohen's/Fleiss' kappa). Accuracy was assessed in an independent 200-encounter cohort (150 random, 50 enriched for rare findings); 100 were double-read by two blinded reviewers with discordances adjudicated. Results: Test-retest reproducibility was high (Tier 1 Fleiss' kappa = 0.993; 99.8% exact) and stable nine weeks later (kappa = 0.992); inter-model agreement was kappa = 0.962. Against the adjudicated reference, pooled Tier 1 accuracy was 0.971 to 0.988 across models (Cohen's kappa 0.959 to 0.982), comparable to inter-reviewer agreement (kappa = 0.932). Accuracy was 0.980 to 0.983 in random and 0.955 to 0.977 in enriched encounters (agreement on model-flagged findings, not sensitivity). Discussion: A decomposed LLM pipeline produced reproducible, model-portable, stable, and accurate multimodal abstraction. Because schema design and validation are up-front costs, such pipelines scale to larger research cohorts. Conclusion: The quantified per-field error rates support reuse of this dataset with field-specific review, and such pipelines offer a practical path to large-scale, reproducible research datasets.

papers.title: Sex shapes plasma molecular signatures of dementia risk across APOE ε4 strata
papers.abstract: Sex and APOE {varepsilon}4 influence dementia risk, but whether its molecular predictors differ across sex and APOE {varepsilon}4 strata remains unclear. We investigated plasma proteomic and metabolomic signatures predicting future dementia in 43,759 UK Biobank participants across four sex-by-APOE {varepsilon}4 groups. The association between APOE {varepsilon}4 carrier status and dementia differed by sex (interaction p = 0.027). Machine-learning models achieved higher discrimination in APOE {varepsilon}4 carriers (AUC 0.85-0.90) than non-carriers (AUC 0.74-0.76), with the highest performance in female carriers. Most top molecular predictors were subgroup-specific, including C7, CDON and EDIL3 in female carriers and KLK4, MMP12 and TGFBI in male carriers. When UK Biobank models were applied to the Global Neurodegeneration Proteomics Consortium, 12/17 available top predictors in female carriers and 10/16 in male carriers remained highly ranked. These findings identify distinct molecular signatures of dementia risk across sex and APOE {varepsilon}4 strata, supporting stratified biomarker discovery.

papers.title: Challenges in Quantifying Upper Extremity Dysmetria in the Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (SARA)
papers.abstract: Background Assessments of upper extremity control in ataxia are susceptible to measurement error and inherent variability. Objectives Quantify trial-to-trial variability in the Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (SARA) nose-to-finger (NTF) and finger chase (FC) tasks, and test agreement between scores derived from live assessment and retrospective video review. Methods 17 patients with cerebellar ataxia were video-recorded performing tasks behind a transparent, calibrated 1-cm grid. NTF tremor amplitude and FC undershoot/overshoot distance derived from live scores were compared with measurements from video review. Results NTF tremor amplitude and FC under/overshoot varied between consecutive trials. Patients received 2.4 {+/-} 0.7 (NTF) and 2.6 {+/-} 0.8 (FC) different SARA scores for limb excursions within one session. Live and video score match was NTF: 64.7% left, 70.6% right; FC: 64.7% left, 41.2% right. Live scoring often overestimated impairment. Conclusions Trial-to-trial variability and live/video discordance limit the precision of SARA upper-limb tasks.

papers.title: Validation of CSF αSyn-SAA in an autopsy cohort with whole-body assessment of Lewy pathology
papers.abstract: Background & Objectives: As recently recommended by neuropathologists, we assessed the diagnostic accuracy of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) alpha-synuclein (-syn) seed amplification assay (SAA) in an autopsy cohort with systemic assessment of Lewy pathology. Methods: CSF was obtained antemortem and stored at -80 . -syn SAA and systemic Lewy pathology assessment were conducted as previously reported. Kinetic parameters, including maximum fluorescence (Fmax) and time to reach 50% of Fmax (T50), were also evaluated. Results: CSF samples were available from 30 patients (8 with symptomatic Lewy body disease [LBD], 2 with multiple system atrophy [MSA], 3 with Alzheimer's disease [AD], and 17 disease controls). Despite different clinical stages, all patients with LBD had diffuse neocortical or limbic-stage pathology at autopsy, with widespread peripheral Lewy bodies, including in the esophagus, heart, and sympathetic ganglia. Lewy pathology was not observed in disease controls. SAA was positive in all 8 with LBD, low positive in one patient with AD, and negative in all others. Fmax was significantly higher in LBD compared with cases without -syn pathology (9091{+/-}2083 vs. 1659{+/-}113 relative fluorescence units). The low-positive case had a lower positivity rate (25% vs. 75-100%), lower Fmax, and longer T50 than LBD cases. Conclusions: In this pilot study, CSF -syn SAA demonstrated high specificity (95%) and high sensitivity (100%) for detecting LBD; however, all LBD cases had widespread pathology, including peripheral involvement. Larger studies are needed to understand the association between CSF -syn SAA and Lewy pathology in the body.

papers.title: MERIT: Multi-agent EHR-grounded Risk Identification and Tailored Care for Early Cognitive Decline in Primary Care
papers.abstract: Background: Dementia is frequently underdiagnosed in primary care, with fewer than half of cases identified and only 8-20% detected at early stages. Our objective is to develop an Agentic AI-powered clinical decision support systems (CDSS) maintaining the patient's virtual cognitive status and provide physicians with ready-to-use summaries and next step suggestions. Methods: We developed MERIT (Multi-agent EHR-grounded Risk Identification and Tailored Care for Early Cognitive Decline in Primary Care) via participatory co-design with primary care provider. It maintains a virtual cognitive status based on the patient's electronic health records (EHR) and conversation with the patient and provide clinical decision support based on it. Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) was employed by the system to retrieve dementia-related risk factors from multimodal EHR. Additionally, we used reflection Agentic AI design pattern to improve quality of AI Agent generated text. We used one PCP's patient data to optimize the system, then used patients from another four PCPs for testing. We mainly used expert manual evaluation based on 5-point Likert-Scales. For readability of patient summary and personalized education material, besides manual evaluation, we also employed widely used Flesch Reading Ease and Flesch We-Kincaid Grade Level. Results: MERIT has four modulars: 1) patient conversation agent; 2) patient virtual cognitive status maintainer; 3) personalized education provider; and 4) decision support provider. Our evaluation focused on the provider-facing part, which relies on EHR without involving any patient conversation. The evaluation on the testing data demonstrates good performance. On a 5-point Likert scale, in the test set, patient virtual cognitive status summaries received average scores of 4.0 (SD 0.74) for correctness, 4.2 (SD 0.59) for completeness, 4.3 (SD 0.59) for readability, and 4.1 (SD 0.71) for clinical usefulness; clinical decision support received 3.9 (SD 0.87) for correctness, 4.3 (SD 0.66) for completeness, and 4.3 (SD 0.64) for adoptability; and the personalized education material received average ratings of 4.3 (SD 0.62) for completeness, 4.5 (SD 0.60) for readability, 4.3 (SD 0.78) for usefulness, and 4.4 (SD 0.49) for empathy. Automated readability assessment showed that patient summaries had a mean Flesch Reading Ease score of 18.3 (SD 4.9) and a Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of 13.7 (SD 0.7), consistent with college-level text, whereas personalized patient education had a Flesch Reading Ease score of 50.1 (SD 7.1) and a Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of 11.7 (SD 1.5), which is high-school student understandable text. Conclusion: Our developed system MERIT can maintain a virtual cognitive status based on the patient's multimodal EHR, provide the patient with clear and readable personalized education materials, and provide the PCP with ready-to-use cognitive summaries and decision support with high adoptability. By integrating our CDSS into Epic in the near future, our developed system will largely benefit older adults with cognitive decline and slow down the progression.

papers.title: Assessment of Dissemination in Time in Multiple Sclerosis Using a Single 3D T2-FLAIR magnetic resonance imaging Radiomic Signature
papers.abstract: Background: In multiple sclerosis (MS), dissemination in time (DIT) is an important component of demonstrating disease activity and establishing the chronology of lesion development. DIT is routinely assessed from contrast-enhanced or follow-up magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Although proved useful, these methods are not without caveats motivating alternative approaches to study lesion chronology. We investigated whether single T2-FLAIR MRI contains sufficient information to distinguish temporally distinct MS lesion categories using radiomic features. Methods: In a retrospective longitudinal cohort of 273 participants with MS (1,311 MRI acquisitions), persistent brain lesions were temporally stratified using serial T2-FLAIR MRI. Long-standing established (LS-E) lesions were defined as observed for six years at least, and recent incident (R-I), as lesions that appeared over the span of two years in a follow-up MRI and were present until the last scan available. Radiomic features were extracted from lesion-level T2-FLAIR MRI. Feature selection was performed in an independent discovery cohort (Group 1, N=55). Selected features were then used to train a support vector machine classifier in a separate development cohort with repeated group-wise cross-validation (Group 2, N=163). Final performance was assessed in an held-out test cohort (Group 3, N=55). An exploratory analysis was then performed on baseline MRI from 64 subjects with clinically isolated syndrome (CIS), acquired after their first clinical demyelinating event. Results: Longitudinal tracking identified 814 classifiable lesions in Group 1, 3203 in Group 2, and 984 in Group 3. In Group 1, 18 radiomic features met predefined selection criteria (FDR-adjusted p smaller than 0.05 and absolute Cohen's d greater than 0.8), spanning intensity, shape, and texture domains. In the independent test cohort, the support vector machine classifier achieved an area under the curve of 0.78, with correct classification rates of 66% for R-I lesions and 73% for LS-E lesions. In the exploratory CIS analysis, predicted lesion temporal composition showed substantial inter-patient heterogeneity, with approximately one in ten participants presenting radiomic features compatible with LS-E lesions at their first clinical event. Conclusions: Single T2-FLAIR MRI contains measurable information related to MS lesion chronology. This proof-of-concept framework supports the feasibility of a line of research based on radiomics temporal lesion characterisation without contrast administration or dense longitudinal follow-up MRI, with potential relevance for studying lesion evolution and supporting DIT assessment.

papers.title: Diagnostic Feature Associations in Atypical Parkinsonian Disorders: A Survey of Movement Disorders Specialists
papers.abstract: Objective: For the atypical parkinsonian disorders (APDs), including dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), multiple system atrophy (MSA), progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), and corticobasal degeneration (CBD), accurate antemortem diagnosis remains clinically challenging because of overlapping features, phenotypic heterogeneity, and limited definitive biomarkers. Consensus diagnostic criteria are complex and may not reflect how clinicians operationalize diagnostic reasoning in practice. Methods: We surveyed movement disorders specialists regarding diagnostic implications of 32 clinical features, comparing the results with a 2024 consensus algorithmic framework called the "General Neurologist's Practical Diagnostic Algorithm for APDs". We evaluated inter-rater agreement, diagnosis-level framework coverage, feature-level attribution patterns, and exact-set agreement. Results: Respondents demonstrated strong inter-specialist consensus in feature attribution (raw agreement 81.9%; Gwet's AC1 0.67, 95% CI 0.64-0.70). Specialist endorsement increased markedly with framework association strength, from 12.9% to 36.2% to 82.6% for unmapped, modest, and moderate associations respectively. Diagnosis-level coverage was higher for MSA, PSP, and CBD than for DLB. Exact-set agreement was substantially more variable and depended on whether modest associations were incorporated into the framework definition. Despite high self-reported familiarity with and use of published diagnostic criteria, respondents overwhelmingly expressed interest in a unified diagnostic framework for APDs with automated clinical decision support (CDS). Conclusions: Movement disorders specialists showed internally consistent feature-attribution patterns for archetypal features, while differing in the weighting and breadth assigned to weaker or overlapping associations. These findings are evidence for a gap between consensus schemas and specialist diagnostic reasoning and may inform future diagnostic frameworks and CDS approaches for the APDs.

papers.title: Quantitative deep motor phenotyping of 102 people with SCN2A, KCNQ2, CSNK2A1, CACNA1A or SCN8A-related disorders
papers.abstract: Background and Objectives: Motor dysfunction is a major contributor to disability in pediatric-onset monogenic neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), yet systematic quantifications of motor phenotypes across development using validated clinical scales remain underdeveloped. Existing studies have classified motor phenotypes rather than quantified domain-specific severity, limiting their use as outcome measures in clinical trials. Here, we systematically quantify motor dysfunction using established clinical rating scales to explore their utility as motor endpoints. Methods: In this cross-sectional observational study, 102 individuals with NDDs (0.5-38 years) secondary to pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in five genes (SCN2A, KCNQ2, CSNK2A1, CACNA1A, SCN8A) and 31 unaffected sibling controls underwent standardized motor assessments using the Scale for Assessment and Rating of Ataxia, Burke-Fahn-Marsden Dystonia Scale, and the Modified Ashworth Scale. Regional and functional categorization of parameters enabled differentiated interpretation. Gene-specific patterns were evaluated using z-score standardization across the pooled affected cohort, with gene-level averaging and nonparametric bootstrap-derived 95% confidence intervals. Results: Dysfunction was present in individuals with NDDs across speech (90%), coordination (87%), dystonia (83.3%), gross motor (82.4%) and spasticity (42.2%), with minimal impairment in controls (0-12.9%). We observed substantial heterogeneity across motor domains and subdomains; ataxic dysarthria had the highest score distribution (median 0.83 [IQR, 0.17-1.0]), whereas spasticity showed near-floor scores. Individuals with SCN2A variants demonstrated higher mean z-scores across multiple subdomains than other genes, with more consistent deviations observed in coordination and speech domains (Coordination: mean z = 0.29, 95% CI 0.03-0.54; Speech: mean z = 0.3, 95% CI 0.03-0.57), whereas domain-specific or less pronounced patterns were observed in other genes. The ataxia and dystonia scales demonstrated low floor and ceiling effects. Discussion: Using three clinical scales across a broad developmental and functional range, our study moves motor phenotyping in monogenic NDDs from categorical description toward quantitative, domain-resolved severity assessment. Exploratory analysis indicates marked heterogeneity in severity profiles across genes, most notably in SCN2A, suggesting potential selective motor vulnerability. These findings provide evidence for the feasibility of motor phenotyping and provide preliminary, cross-sectional benchmark severity distributions. Subsequent longitudinal validation and validation in larger, longitudinal, and variant-stratified cohorts will enable natural history studies and future therapeutic trials alongside seizure outcomes.

papers.title: Enhancing deep sleep with auditory stimulation to boost cognitive training responsiveness in people with Parkinson's disease and mild cognitive impairment: Rationale and design of the double-blind randomized controlled trial PD-CogT-Sleep
papers.abstract: Background: Cognitive training (CogT) is an established non-pharmacological intervention for people with Parkinson's disease (PD) and mild cognitive impairment (PD-MCI). However, overall effects on cognitive outcomes are small to moderate and interindividually highly heterogeneous. Sleep -especially deep sleep- could be an important determinant of CogT responsiveness in PD, and may have beneficial effects on PD pathophysiology. Therefore, the enhancement of deep sleep by phase-targeted auditory stimulation (PTAS) could strengthen the effects of CogT on cognitive symptoms and counteract disease progression. Methods: PD-CogT-Sleep is a monocentric, partly decentralized, double-blind, randomized sham-controlled trial that combines two remotely delivered non-pharmacological interventions, to assess the additive effect of PTAS on digital CogT responsiveness in people with PD-MCI. The primary outcome is executive functions; Secondary and exploratory outcomes include further cognitive functions, participant-reported outcome measures, blood-based biomarkers, and high-density sleep electroencephalography markers. Outcomes are assessed at baseline, five weeks post-allocation and at 3-month follow-up. We aim to consecutively recruit N=50 participants, who will be randomized 1:1 to receive CogT+PTAS or CogT+Sham. Discussion: The PD-CogT-Sleep study integrates wearable and digital technologies to systematically combine a novel, non-invasive, sleep-enhancing intervention (PTAS) with established CogT to improve cognition and evaluate PTAS' disease-modifying potential through its effects on blood-based biomarkers in PD-MCI. The expected results will foster our understanding of the interplay of sleep, cognition, and neurodegeneration, and may guide further development of safe, feasible, scalable, patient-centered, technology-based non-pharmacological interventions counteracting cognitive decline in neurodegenerative diseases.

papers.title: Multi-ancestry rare variant burden analysis of E3 ubiquitin ligase genes in Parkinson's disease
papers.abstract: E3 ubiquitin ligases regulate protein degradation through the ubiquitin-proteasome system and have been implicated in early-onset Parkinsons disease (EOPD). We performed a multi-ancestry rare-variant burden analysis of seven E3 ubiquitin ligase genes (HERC1, IRF2BPL, KMT2D, RAPSN, RNF168, RNF216, TRIM2) using GP2 Release 11 WGS data from 17,928 PD patients (including 6,659 EOPD) and 8,977 controls across five major ancestry groups (African, Central Asian, East Asian, European, and Middle Eastern). We did not identify any association between gene based rare burden and PD, using the optimised sequence kernel association test (SKAT-O).

papers.title: Head-to-Head Comparison of Flortaucipir and MK6240 tau-PET to Detect Subtle Objective Cognitive Impairment in Clinically Unimpaired Individuals
papers.abstract: Background and ObjectivesTau-PET is associated with subtle objective cognitive impairment (SOCI) in clinically unimpaired (CU) individuals, but whether the spatial patterns and strengths of these associations differ across tracers remains unclear. We performed a head-to-head comparison of [{superscript 1}{square}F]MK6240 and [{superscript 1}{square}F]flortaucipir to investigate their associations with SOCI in CU individuals. MethodsWe cross-sectionally assessed CU participants from the HEAD study who underwent both tau-PET scans. Linear regressions examined associations between domain-specific cognition and tau burden using standardized uptake value ratios (SUVR) in regional and voxelwise analyses, alongside regional spatial extent of tauopathy (SEOT) measures. Tau burden was compared across groups representing different levels of SOCI. Models adjusted for age, sex, and education, with additional adjustment for amyloid-{beta} burden. Centiloid-stratified analyses examined associations across amyloid-{beta} burden levels. ResultsAmong 297 participants (mean [SD] age, 67.0 [8.4] years; 179 [60.3%] female), higher [{superscript 1}{square}F]MK6240 SUVR was associated with poorer memory performance. Greater SEOT with either tracer was associated with poorer memory and showed nominal associations with executive dysfunction. Regional association strengths did not differ significantly between tracers, while SEOT yielded comparable or stronger associations than SUVR. Centiloid-stratified analyses revealed tau- cognition associations primarily at intermediate and high amyloid-{beta} burden. [{superscript 1}{square}F]MK6240 showed more spatially extensive voxelwise associations with memory and across SOCI group comparisons. Regional analyses also yielded more statistically significant differences across SOCI groups with [{superscript 1}{square}F]MK6240 than with flortaucipir. These differences were predominantly driven by participants meeting actuarial mild cognitive impairment criteria, who exhibited greater tau burden than groups with less pronounced psychometric impairment. Across tracers, SEOT yielded more consistently significant differences among SOCI groups than SUVR. DiscussionBoth tracers showed associations with SOCI in CU individuals, with broadly comparable regional association strengths despite differences in the spatial extent and statistical significance of their findings. SEOT complemented SUVR by identifying additional significant associations and group differences. These findings suggest that tracer choice and quantification approach may influence the spatial distribution and statistical significance of observed tau-cognition relationships without necessarily altering their overall strength.

papers.title: Tau PET Braak staging across the Alzheimer Disease continuum using Flortaucipir and MK6240
papers.abstract: Tau positron emission tomography (PET) staging is increasingly used to stratify Alzheimers disease (AD), yet cross-tracer interchangeability remains unestablished. In a prospective head-to-head study of 682 individuals across the aging-to-AD continuum, we compared tau PET Braak staging derived from [18F]Flortaucipir and [18F]MK6240. While both tracers showed high internal adherence to hierarchical Braak patterns (89-92%), cross-tracer agreement was limited (43%, weighted {kappa} = 0.54) and fell to 14- 23% at early-to-intermediate stages, a key window for therapeutic intervention. Discordance was strongly directional: in over 90% of discordant cases [18F]MK6240 assigned a higher stage, on average approximately one stage above [18F]Flortaucipir. [18F]MK6240 upstaging was associated with greater A{beta} burden, adverse plasma biomarker profiles, and worse cognitive performance. Stage-frequency benchmarking against an external neuropathological cohort (N = 4,422) revealed that PET staging lags neuropathology by [~]2 Braak stages for [18F]MK6240 and [~]3 for [18F]Flortaucipir in the early phases of disease, with progressive convergence at later stages. Tau PET Braak staging is internally coherent within tracers but not interchangeable across them, with [18F]MK6240 systematically assigning higher stages than [18F]Flortaucipir. This biologically meaningful discordance, most pronounced at early stages, has direct implications for patient selection and staging for clinical trials and practice, necessitating tracer- aware harmonization strategies.

papers.title: Benchmarking single-subject detectability of cognitive event-related potentials in healthy controls and minimally conscious state patients
papers.abstract: Event-related potentials (ERP) may reveal residual cognitive processing in disorders of consciousness, but clinical translation is limited because group-level effects do not guarantee reliable single-subject detection. Few ERP paradigms have been benchmarked in healthy participants and compared directly with patients in disorders of consciousness. We tested a hierarchical ERP battery in healthy controls and patients in minimally conscious state (MCS) to (1) estimate upper-bound single-subject detectability in healthy participants, (2) compare detection rates with those of MCS patients, and (3) evaluate prognostic value for recovery of consciousness. Forty-eight healthy controls and 26 patients in MCS completed six auditory paradigms: multifeature mismatch negativity (MMN), passive and active oddball P300, the subjects own name, semantic oddball, and sentence N400. Effects were classified using blinded expert visual scoring, region-of-interest ANOVA, cluster-based permutation tests, and support vector machine decoding. Associations between binary ERP classifications and recovery were tested in 22 surviving patients at follow-up. In healthy controls, visual scoring identified MMN to at least one deviant and P300 in both oddball tasks in all 48 participants. Command following as demonstrated by task-related P300 enhancement between active and passive oddball conditions was detected in 81%. Command following was detected in 92% in the semantic oddball task. Sentence-congruity effects (N400 and/or P600) were identified in 69%, despite a strong group-level response, while the own-name effect was detected in only 35%. In patients, detection rates were lower: MMN was found in 27% for the short-duration deviant and 65% when any of five deviant types counted as positive; passive oddball P300 in 35% and active oddball P300 in 31%; sentence-congruity effects in 12%; active-versus-passive oddball modulation in 12%; and semantic oddball effects in 8%. Visual scoring and machine learning generally detected more effects than ANOVA and cluster-based testing, and agreement varied substantially across paradigms. Binary ERP classifications were not significantly associated with recovery (14 recovered, eight did not), although prognostic analyses were limited by sample size. Group-level ERP effects overstated single-subject detectability in healthy controls, whereas the absence of group-level effects in MCS obscured reliable ERP responses resembling those of healthy controls in a few individual patients. In MCS, ERP effects associated with semantic processing and command following were generally uncommon, and binary ERP indicators did not predict recovery in this sample. Our findings establish a benchmark for selecting and refining ERP paradigms and detection methods to assess residual cognition after severe brain injury.

papers.title: Alzheimers disease and psychiatric polygenic risk are disease-specific and independent of plasma biomarkers in a real-world young-onset dementia cohort.
papers.abstract: Background: Young onset dementia is frequently misdiagnosed, particularly where neurodegenerative and primary psychiatric disorders (PPD) overlap. Plasma biomarkers measure current pathology, whereas polygenic risk scores (PRS) capture lifelong genetic risk. Whether PRS derived from late-onset and population samples transfer to young-onset presentations, and how they relate to plasma biomarkers, is unknown. Methods: We studied 687 participants of European ancestry from the Markers in Neuropsychiatric Disorders (MiND) Study, a prospective young-onset neuropsychiatry cohort: 195 healthy controls (HC), 283 PPD, 55 Alzheimers disease (AD) and 154 non-AD neurodegenerative disease (oNDG). PRS for AD, a cross-disorder psychiatric factor (PSY), frontotemporal dementia, Lewy body dementia and Parkinsons disease were computed with PRS CS, excluding the APOE locus. Plasma NfL, GFAP and p-tau217 were available for 332 participants. Models were adjusted for age, sex and APOE e4 dose. Results: Relative to HC, the AD PRS was associated with AD (OR 1.69 per SD, 95% CI 1.17-2.45) but not PPD (0.95, 0.77-1.16). The PSY PRS showed the reciprocal pattern (PPD 1.29, 1.05-1.58; AD 1.00, 0.72-1.40). No PRS was associated with any plasma protein. In distinguishing PPD from oNDG, NfL was the strongest discriminator (OR 2.15, 1.62-2.83). The AD PRS was also associated with oNDG (1.38, 1.11-1.71), without improving discrimination (AUC 0.764 for NfL alone versus 0.773 combined). Conclusion: In young onset presentations, AD and psychiatric polygenic risk are disease-specific and independent of plasma biomarkers of neurodegeneration. Their combined diagnostic value requires evaluation in larger, longitudinal pre-clinical cohorts.

papers.title: Short intervals of inertial measurement unit data collected during activities of daily living can provide a quantitative method to assess disease severity and functional ability in Parkinson's disease
papers.abstract: Parkinsons disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder affecting roughly one million people in the U.S. People with PD (PwPD) exhibit classic motor symptoms that limit performance on functional tasks and reduce quality of life (QOL). Despite functional ability (FA) being a critical indicator of patient well-being, objective and quantitative measurement of FA during activities of daily living (ADLs) is not a part of standard clinical assessments. To address this gap, we conducted a pilot study of PwPD (n=39) and healthy controls (n=7) performing ADLs. We attached nine-axis inertial measurement units (IMUs) to toothbrushes and hair combs to collect continuous acceleration and angular velocity data during toothbrushing and hair-combing tasks. After preprocessing, we visualized signals with kernel density estimation and continuous wavelet transforms, revealing characteristic distributional, temporal, and spectral patterns. We then segmented signals into 3-9 second non-overlapping intervals. From each interval, we extracted 30 features (13 acceleration-derived, 17 angular-velocity-derived) and trained eXtreme Gradient Boosted (XGBoost) classifiers to discriminate disease state and severity, symptom presence, and impaired FA. Notably, models trained on hair-combing data discriminated PwPD from controls (balanced accuracy 0.864) and identified patient-reported impairment in FA (0.869). Models trained on toothbrushing data achieved moderate performance on the same tasks (balanced accuracy 0.752 and 0.686, respectively). These preliminary findings suggest that short-segment IMU data from common ADL implements can quantitatively characterize disease severity and task-specific performance in PwPD, supporting their integration into routine clinical care.

papers.title: Increased variability in visual processing in children with autism
papers.abstract: The visual evoked potential (VEP) indexes sensory processing, but the neurophysiological basis of altered VEP amplitudes in autism remains unclear. We examined whether reduced VEP amplitude reflects increased trial-to-trial neural variability and whether this variability relates to electrophysiological markers of cortical excitation/inhibition and developmental functioning. Pattern-reversal VEPs were analyzed in 102 typically developing (TD; 44 female) and 105 autistic (AUT; 15 female) children aged 2-12 years. N1 and N1-P1 amplitudes and inter-trial phase coherence (ITPC) were computed. Resting-state periodic alpha activity and aperiodic exponent were derived using spectral parameterization. Associations among VEP, resting EEG, age, and developmental/behavioral measures were assessed using multiple linear regression. AUT children exhibited reduced N1 amplitude and lower ITPC, with marginally reduced N1-P1 amplitude. Higher ITPC was strongly associated with larger N1 and N1-P1 amplitudes, and group differences in VEP amplitudes were no longer significant after accounting for ITPC. Greater periodic alpha activity was associated with higher ITPC and larger N1-P1 amplitude, while a steeper aperiodic exponent was associated with higher ITPC in the pooled cohort. Within AUT children, higher ITPC was associated with better nonverbal development, verbal cognition, and language scores. Reduced VEP amplitudes in autism may primarily reflect increased trial-to-trial variability rather than systematically weaker stimulus-evoked responses. Associations between ITPC and resting EEG measures suggest that cortical excitation/inhibition may contribute to sensory response reliability. These findings identify neural response consistency as a developmentally relevant feature of visual processing in autism.

papers.title: Clinically Meaningful Cognitive Improvement from Intermittent Neurostimulation of the Nucleus Basalis of Meynert in Parkinson's Disease
papers.abstract: Cognitive decline begins in early stages of Parkinsons disease (PD) for many individuals and remains largely untreated. The nucleus basalis of Meynert (NBM), the brains cortical cholinergic hub, and its lateral efferent fiber bundle degenerate early in PD and are linked to cognitive and cognitive-motor impairment. Pre-clinical evidence indicates intermittent stimulation of the NBM improves cognition. The objective of this study is to establish the feasibility of combined continuous subthalamic nucleus (STN) and intermittent NBM DBS for cognitive impairment in people with PD. Five patients with PD and cognitive impairment approved for STN DBS were enrolled as part of an ongoing clinical trial for combined STN and NBM DBS under an Investigational Device Exemption. Three participants received a vertical trajectory in which two leads were placed in the STN, and two additional leads were placed in the anterior portion of the NBM, both using the same burr hole for each hemisphere. The two other participants received a novel lateral trajectory in which the NBM leads were placed along the NBM lateral efferent bundle via a small twist craniostomy behind the ear. An automated programming algorithm DBS Illumina 3D (Boston Scientific) was used to program the NBM leads based on volume of tissue activated modeling. The investigational Chronos software (Boston Scientific) was used to deliver continuous high frequency DBS to the STN 24 hours/day and intermittent patterned DBS to the NBM for 1 hour/day. The two leads placed in the NBM ( Vertical target) or its lateral efferent bundle ( Lateral target) were successfully and accurately placed as part of the usual STN DBS procedure. All participants were successfully programmed using the Illumina 3D algorithm without adverse effects. Following 6 months of combined continuous STN and intermittent NBM DBS, all five participants saw clinically meaningful improvements in cognition as part of a neuropsychological assessment battery, as well as the expected motoric benefit from STN DBS. The current study demonstrated that intermittent stimulation of the NBM to target cortical cholinergic deficits may provide clinically meaningful improvements in cognitive symptoms in Parkinsons disease. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05968703

papers.title: High-frequency EEG activity moderates the association between amyloid burden and tau in cognitively normal adults
papers.abstract: BackgroundResting electroencephalogram (EEG) may capture early excitatory-inhibitory (E-I) imbalance in Alzheimers disease, but its relationship to beta-amyloid (A{beta}) and tau in cognitively normal adults is unclear. MethodsWe analyzed resting-state EEG from 24 older adults: 21 cognitively normal (13 A{beta}-negative, 8 A{beta}-positive) and 3 with MCI/AD (all A{beta}-positive), with A{beta} positron emission tomography (PET); 20 cognitively normal adults also had tau PET. Four parietal EEG measures reflecting excitation-inhibition (E-I) balance and neuronal excitability (periodic gamma power, alpha-gamma and theta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling [PAC], and the aperiodic exponent) were assessed for associations with A{beta} burden and early medial temporal lobe (MTL) tau, adjusting for age and sex. ResultsIn 21 cognitively normal adults, higher A{beta} burden was associated with higher parietal periodic gamma power ({beta} = +0.50, p = 0.025). No E-I measure was associated with MTL tau across all participants. However, in A{beta}-positive adults, higher periodic gamma was associated with higher MTL tau, most strongly in the entorhinal cortex ({rho} = +0.90, p = 0.002), with no association in A{beta}-negative adults. Importantly, periodic gamma also moderated the association between A{beta} and MTL tau (p = 0.012; consistent across MTL regions after FDR correction). ConclusionsIn this pilot study, parietal periodic gamma, an EEG marker of cortical excitability, increased with A{beta} burden and was related to MTL tau only in the presence of A{beta}. Periodic gamma power may serve as a candidate marker of A{beta}-associated E-I imbalance and early AD progression.

papers.title: Benefit Expectations and Neuroprotective Prescribing for Acute Ischemic Stroke in China
papers.abstract: BackgroundNeuroprotective therapies are frequently used for acute ischemic stroke in China. We examined associations of neurologists self-rated familiarity, perceived importance, and benefit expectations with reported prescribing frequency. MethodsA hospital-based quota survey recruited attending-level or senior neurologists involved in acute ischemic stroke care across mainland China from May 27 to July 16, 2025. High-frequency use was defined as prescribing neuroprotective therapy to at least 60% of patients. High familiarity and importance were ratings of 4 or 5 on 5-level scales; consistently high benefit expectations required ratings of 4 or 5 in all 4 scenarios. Modified Poisson generalized estimating equations estimated adjusted prevalence ratios (PRs) with hospital-clustered robust standard errors. ResultsAmong 1982 neurologists from 251 hospitals, 1007 (50.8%) were men and 1745 (88.0%) practiced in tertiary hospitals. High-frequency use was reported by 1596 respondents (80.5%), high familiarity by 1006 (50.8%), and consistently high benefit expectations by 1290 (65.1%). Lower familiarity with high-frequency use was reported by 743 respondents (37.5%). High familiarity (adjusted PR, 1.053; 95% CI, 1.007-1.102), high perceived importance (adjusted PR, 1.294; 95% CI, 1.148-1.458), and consistently high benefit expectations (adjusted PR, 1.198; 95% CI, 1.131-1.269) were associated with high-frequency use after adjustment for demographic and professional characteristics. ConclusionsFrequent self-reported neuroprotective prescribing coexisted with lower self-rated familiarity in a substantial subgroup. Familiarity, perceived importance, and benefit expectations were associated with prescribing frequency. These cross-sectional, class-level measures cannot establish prescribing appropriateness or causality. Studies linking drug-specific observed prescribing to indications and patient outcomes are needed.

papers.title: Repetitive negative thinking is associated with amyloid accumulation over 3 years in cognitively healthy adults
papers.abstract: ImportanceIdentifying potentially modifiable risk factors for Alzheimers disease (AD) is a priority. Repetitive negative thinking (RNT) is a modifiable cognitive-emotional process common to many psychological risk factors for AD, including anxiety and depression. The psychological debt hypothesis proposes that RNT may itself increase risk for AD. ObjectiveTo determine whether RNT symptoms are associated with change in established neurobiological markers of AD risk over time. DesignLongitudinal neuroimaging study with the IMAP/IMAP+ cohort. SettingMonocentric with community-dwelling participants. Participants94 cognitively healthy adults aged 21-89 years (average 57.41 SD 18.31, 55% female) with up to 3 neuroimaging scans over a 3-year period. ExposureAll participants completed validated measures of RNT, anxiety and depression symptoms. Main Outcome(s) and Measure(s)Change over time in global cortical amyloid (Florbetapir-PET), glucose metabolism (FDG-PET), and structural grey matter volume (MRI) adjusted for potential confounders. PET images were corrected for partial volume effects, and AD-relevant masks were used for all neuroimaging outcomes. Post-hoc analyses divided the predictor variable into tertiles to aid visualisation, and FDR-corrected voxel-wise analyses were performed to identify region-specific changes. ResultsRNT was associated with increasing global amyloid accumulation even after controlling for psychological symptoms (B = 0.0120, 95% Confidence Interval 0.003 to 0.021, P = 0.012), and in sensitivity analyses limited to participants aged [≥]50 or [≥]60. Post-hoc tests showed a significant difference in rate of amyloid accumulation between the lowest and highest RNT tertiles (P=0.008). Voxelwise analyses revealed that RNT predicted significantly faster increases in regions vulnerable to early amyloid accumulation in AD (e.g. precuneus, posterior cingulate cortex, and medial frontal cortex). RNT was not associated with change in glucose metabolism or brain atrophy (Ps>0.05). Neither anxiety nor depressive symptoms were associated with change in any neuroimaging outcome (Ps>0.05). Conclusions and RelevanceHigher RNT was associated with more rapid accumulation of cortical amyloid in regions affected early in AD. These findings indicate that this transdiagnostic cognitive-emotional process may be an early marker and/or driver of AD pathology. Given that RNT is responsive to treatment, future research is needed to investigate whether modifying RNT reduces AD risk.

papers.title: Relative Importance of Positive and Potentially Traumatic Childhood Experiences in Explaining Multiple Sclerosis Symptoms
papers.abstract: The original adverse childhood experiences study linked childhood experiences to health in adulthood. Since then, other traumatic and adverse childhood experiences (TRACEs) and positive childhood experiences (PCEs) have also been linked to physical and mental health. However, little research has examined these experiences among people with Multiple Sclerosis (MS). This study examined whether cumulative and individual childhood experiences explained variability in symptom burden in adults with MS. Participants were 467 adults with MS (Mage = 41.5, 45% female) who completed measures of pain, subjective cognitive impairment, cognitive fatigue, depression, TRACEs, and PCEs. The elastic net algorithm examined cumulative TRACEs, PCEs, their interaction, and individual childhood experiences. R-squared was used to assess the proportion of variance in each outcome accounted for by childhood experiences, and variable importance identified experiences that most improved the models explanatory power for each outcome. Individual childhood experiences accounted for 26.0%, 17.1%, 13.9%, and 22.4% of variance in pain, subjective cognitive impairment, cognitive fatigue, and depression, respectively, and overall had stronger performance relative to the cumulative main effects TRACEs and PCEs model, and their interaction. Having at least one safe caregiver was consistently important across MS symptoms, and sudden loss of a loved one had the strongest explanatory association with subjective cognitive impairment and cognitive fatigue specifically. Specific childhood experiences accounted for meaningful variance in the MS symptom burden. Individual childhood experiences provided more explanatory information than cumulative scores. Findings support examining specific TRACEs and PCEs when investigating symptom burden in MS.
